segments.say: Let the sound of the waves soften, and slowly turn into another sound. A gentle tapping, light and steady, all around you. It's rain. You are inside an old glass greenhouse at the bottom of a quiet garden, and a soft evening rain is falling on the roof. You are dry and warm, surrounded by green, and the whole world outside has grown misty and still.

Listen to the rain on the glass above you. Thousands of tiny taps, never quite in rhythm, never too loud. Some drops land close, some far away. Together they make a soft, endless hush, like someone whispering a lullaby they've known all their life. There's nothing to do but listen. Let the sound settle over you like a light, warm blanket.

The air in here is warm and a little damp, and it smells wonderful. Wet soil. Green leaves. A faint sweetness from somewhere, perhaps a flowering plant you can't quite see. Breathe it in, slowly, through your nose. Hold it for just a moment. And breathe out, long and slow. Again. Each breath is a little deeper, a little calmer, than the one before.

Here is a quiet thought, from the plants around you. Nothing in a garden grows by being hurried. Seeds don't sprout faster because someone stands over them, worrying. Leaves don't open sooner because someone is watching. They grow in their own time, a little each day and a little each night, mostly when nobody is looking at all.

show.text: Nothing in a garden grows by being hurried.

segments.say: Along the wooden benches, there are rows of clay pots, each one holding something small and patient. A young tomato plant with soft, fuzzy leaves. A tray of tiny seedlings, just two leaves each, leaning toward where the light will be in the morning. A trailing plant spilling over the edge of a shelf. Everything here is quietly becoming a little more itself.

In one corner, there's an old wooden chair with a folded blanket on the seat. You walk over slowly, past the benches, brushing a leaf or two with your fingertips. You sit down and pull the blanket over your knees. It's soft and a little heavy, and it smells faintly of cedar. From here you can see the whole greenhouse, glowing softly in the dusk.

Look up at the glass. Raindrops gather on the panes, grow heavier, and then slide slowly down in little winding paths, joining others on the way. Beyond the glass, the garden is soft and blurred, all greens and greys. A small lantern hangs from a hook among the leaves, glowing warm and amber. In here, everything is safe, and dry, and slow.

Look at one of the larger plants nearby. Some of its leaves are bright and new. A few lower ones are older, with a brown edge or a little tear. One has a small curl where it grew around something in its way. And yet the whole plant is healthy and beautiful. The imperfect leaves don't spoil it. They're simply part of its story of growing.

People are a little like that, too. We grow around our clumsy moments, our awkward words, the times we waved at the wrong person or said the wrong thing. They leave tiny curls and marks, and those become part of us, softly. Nobody looks at a plant and sees only its one bent leaf. Most people see the green, and the growing, and the life.

Listen to the rain again, and imagine it's saying a few simple things, over and over. You can stop now. The day is done. Everything is watered. Rest. Let each word fall softly onto you, like a drop on the glass. You can stop now. The day is done. Everything is watered. Rest.

Now, imagine any small thought that's still with you from today, anything you said or did that you'd like to set down. Picture it as one of those raindrops on the glass. Watch it slowly slide down the pane, finding its little path, joining the others, and disappearing into the soil below, where it will quietly help something grow.

Feel how heavy and soft your body has become under the blanket. Your feet are warm. Your legs are still. Your hands rest loosely in your lap. Let your shoulders drop away from your ears. Let your forehead smooth out, as if a cool, kind hand were resting there for a moment. Breathe in the warm, green air. And breathe out, slowly, all the way.

Here's a gentle thought, as the rain keeps falling. Growth mostly happens quietly, in the dark, while you rest. Plants do much of their growing at night. And your mind, too, does some of its gentlest work while you sleep, softening the edges of the day and making room for tomorrow. You don't have to do anything for that to happen. You only need to rest.

show.text: Growth mostly happens quietly, in the dark, while you rest.

segments.say: The little lantern among the leaves glows a little lower now, its light warm and steady and small. The rain keeps its soft rhythm on the roof. Somewhere a drop falls from a leaf onto the soil with a tiny sound, and then another. The greenhouse is breathing slowly with you, warm and damp and green, and completely at peace.

In a little while, the rain will ease, and the clouds will part, and we'll drift up somewhere high and open, under a wide, clear sky full of stars. But for now, stay here in the warm green dark, under the blanket, listening to the rain, breathing slowly, and letting everything grow quietly in its own good time.
